test_title: PYST 37: RRB Group D - GS (Held On: 14 Dec, 2025 Shift 1)
subject: general
question: Which of the following correctly compares the cell wall and cell membrane in plant and animal cells?

options.text: Plant cells have both a rigid cell wall and a cell membrane, while animal cells only have a flexible cell membrane.
Animal cells have both a rigid cell wall and a cell membrane, while plant cells only have a flexible cell membrane.
Both plant and animal cells have a cell wall but only plant cells have a cell membrane.
Neither plant nor animal cells have a cell wall, but both have a cell membrane.

solution: The correct answer is __**Plant cells have both a rigid cell wall and a cell membrane, while animal cells only have a flexible cell membrane.**__. [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__** • **Plant cells** have a **rigid cell wall** made of cellulose, providing structural support and protection. • In addition, plant cells possess a **cell membrane** which is flexible and regulates the transport of substances in and out of the cell. • **Animal cells** lack a cell wall and only have a **flexible cell membrane**, which helps in maintaining shape and controlling substance exchange. • The absence of a cell wall in animal cells makes them more adaptable and allows greater variation in shape compared to plant cells. • The presence of a cell wall in plant cells is essential for maintaining turgidity and resisting osmotic pressure, which is vital for plant survival. *Hence, the statement is correct.*
